findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional two-heap design. It maintains the smaller half as a negated max-heap, the larger half as a min-heap, restores their one-element size bound after every insertion, and reads the correct one- or two-root median. The app driver cleanly returns every running median, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 295 and its Python MedianFinder design surface plus offline stream adapter. The Reference preserves the median definition, constructor and method contracts, tolerance, sole operation-trace example and full explanation, all three constraints, and both distribution follow-ups.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064354914. Its MedianFinder class and the protected app-local class have identical heap initialization, placement, rebalancing, and median logic; the app-only solve driver merely performs each add-and-query pair and collects the results.

The former benchmark used values near plus or minus 1,000,000, outside the source range. Its symmetric alternating sequence and medians are now shifted into the legal plus or minus 100,000 domain while preserving 64/256/1024-operation tiers and all rebalancing behavior. The current source passes at -0.01 relative exponent and 0.98x largest ratio; correct ordered insertion passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.99 and 41.70x.

The Approach derives the ordering and size invariants, explains why moving a boundary root preserves them, defines n before the manifest bounds, accounts for all running queries and heap storage, and separates duplicate, negative, and even-length behavior.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving the sole operation-trace example and explanation, all three constraints, both follow-ups, and the zero-visual structure.
